title: Agent verifier
evidenceStatus: 20 complete requests over five identical authored states repeated four times; 20/20 expected verdicts, no identity flips, score drift in three groups. All 20 evidence scores exist in raw responses but are omitted from published rows. Offline source/wire/callback audit only.
summary: The current verifier is a five-template integration check with stable repeated verdicts, not independent validation of completed work. The recorder drops half its answers, the live protocol differs, and malformed input or late responses can change which evidence is assessed. A versioned proof tray should separate artifact facts, semantic support, scope and uncertainty.
strengths: Authored targets are excluded from model input; complete task/trace/claim text is preserved.
The result explicitly identifies five independent templates and states that the verifier does not authorize tool execution.
All twenty requests completed and repeat identities are stable, with provider attempts and scores retained.

findings.title: Five repeated narratives do not establish completion verification
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/compositions.py:75, :138; experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:452, :465. Five exact state bodies appear four times each; the UI omits the independent-template note. A recorded policy-found trace claims a URL exists but contains no URL.
findings.impact: Twenty row-level successes and calibration summaries overstate evidence breadth if treated as independent problems; narratives cannot authenticate unseen artifacts.
findings.fix: Group repeats visibly, retain the integration-fixture label, and evaluate versioned tool receipts/artifacts with independent checks.

findings.title: Twenty evidence judgments are discarded and live questions differ
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/compositions.py:119, :125; experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:221. probes/verify.json counts 40 raw primitive answers, 20 evidence scores and zero published evidence scores; live requests ask only verdict with changed descriptions.
findings.impact: A useful support diagnostic is lost and the saved examples are not the live protocol.
findings.fix: Retain exact requests and all raw answers, share a versioned question builder, and show diagnostic disagreement without treating it as independent truth.

findings.title: Late verification replaces a newly selected failed trace
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:261, :441. Actual callback probe starts parser verification, selects failed-import example 4, then installs the old verified result while editor/selector remain on import.
findings.impact: The active selection and verdict diverge, though the result still retains its old task/trace.
findings.fix: Bind answers to task/trace/claim revisions and selection generation; show historical judgments separately and reject stale commits.

findings.title: Malformed JSON silently supplies a different completion claim
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:212. An unfinished task/trace object becomes raw trace plus a default success claim; valid [] bypasses shape validation. No model outcomes for these inputs were measured.
findings.impact: Input errors change the assessment contract instead of explaining what evidence is missing.
findings.fix: Separate plain-text/structured modes and validate nonempty task, explicit claim and typed evidence before requesting a verdict.

findings.title: One category conflates scope, outcome and verification
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/compositions.py:113; experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:298. Four exclusive labels mix independent dimensions, and no fixture combines scope violation with failed or successful work.
findings.impact: Overlapping failures and partial completion have no declared summary policy.
findings.fix: Show the claim explicitly, preserve separate support/verification/scope axes and derive a summary under documented precedence with unknowns retained.

simulation.title: A proof tray for one completion claim
simulation.description: Inspect a task, claim and typed receipt timeline; remove or stale one artifact, predict the consequence, and compare Jev's judgment with deterministic checks from the same checkpoint.
simulation.jevsRole: Interpret semantic relevance and whether the claim exceeds the visible evidence.
simulation.codeRole: Validate event schemas, preserve origin/revision hashes, run predefined artifact assertions, enforce scope facts and isolate asynchronous results; never execute commands extracted from trace text.
acceptanceCriteria: Every answer references exact task/claim/evidence versions.
Malformed input triggers no model request.
Passing checks on old artifacts are insufficient under deterministic provenance checks.
Scope and outcome remain separate and unknowns never become verified through missing values.
Late responses cannot replace the active trace; exports retain raw and derived outcomes.

evaluation.design: Create 100 independently authored reproducible task families; use 20 development and 80 held out. Eight trace conditions per task yield 640 held-out traces, covering valid completion, missing/failed/unrelated/stale checks, scope violation, narrative-only success, partial work and combined failure. Two reviewers label semantic relevance/support, while artifact assertions establish outcomes. Three unchanged passes with one verdict plus three axis questions require 1,920 logical requests and 7,680 primitive decisions. Freeze precedence and thresholds; bootstrap by 80 source tasks. Provisional gate: false-verified upper 95% bound below 5%, reporting coverage and useful verification recall. Exercise 1,000 asynchronous integrity schedules over 100 seeds. All proposed runs remain unperformed.
baselines: Structured provenance and deterministic artifact-assertion checker.
metrics: False verified rate and verified recall.
Needs-check precision, scope-violation recall and per-axis agreement.
Summary confusion, benign paraphrase and injection sensitivity, unchanged-repeat flips.
All-scheduled/provider-completed coverage, retries, latency and cost.
Wrong-version commits and invalid-input request count.

coverage.current: Five unique authored state bodies, four repetitions each; no independently executed artifacts or combined-failure cases.
coverage.full: Proposed 640 held-out traces from 80 task families, 1,920 requests/7,680 decisions; 20 development families and 1,000 offline schedules.
coverage.feasibility: Requires independent annotation and reproducible owned artifacts; no external benchmark or official score claimed. Receipt construction is the main setup cost; no dataset/weight download needed.

libraries.use: Already installed; validate distinct tool receipts, agent claims and explicit task/trace schemas.
